pages.quiz:
MUSIC AND DANCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MUSIC AND DANCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Best practice when working on Four-Part Harmony: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Four-Part Harmony.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Four-Part Harmony.
   C. Practise Four-Part Harmony with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Four-Part Harmony.

2. Primary colours are: (1 mark)
   A. Green, orange, and purple
   B. Red, blue, and yellow
   C. Black, white, and grey
   D. Brown, pink, and gold

3. In music, tempo refers to: (1 mark)
   A. The ticket price
   B. Only the costume
   C. Only the volume
   D. The speed of the music

4. Best practice when working on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   B. Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   D. Damage equipment used for Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.

5. Best practice when working on Western Ensembles: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Western Ensembles.
   B. Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Western Ensembles.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Western Ensembles.

6. Best practice when working on Rhythm: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Rhythm.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Rhythm.
   C. Damage equipment used for Rhythm.
   D. Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. Best practice when working on Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.
   C. Practise Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Damage equipment used for Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.

8. Warming up before sport helps to: (1 mark)
   A. Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk
   B. Replace drinking water
   C. Remove the need for rules
   D. Guarantee a trophy

9. Best practice when working on Kenyan Contemporary Songs: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan Contemporary Songs.
   B. Damage equipment used for Kenyan Contemporary Songs.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan Contemporary Songs.
   D. Practise Kenyan Contemporary Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

10. Best practice when working on Contemporary Songs from Kenya: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Contemporary Songs from Kenya.
   B. Damage equipment used for Contemporary Songs from Kenya.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Contemporary Songs from Kenya.
   D. Practise Contemporary Songs from Kenya with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

11. Best practice when working on Western Instruments: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Western Instruments with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Western Instruments.
   C. Damage equipment used for Western Instruments.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Western Instruments.

12. Best practice when working on Instrumental Transpositions: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Instrumental Transpositions.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Instrumental Transpositions.
   C. Damage equipment used for Instrumental Transpositions.
   D. Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Kenyan Contemporary Songs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Classical Music and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Music and Dance Industry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Rhythm and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Practise Four-Part Harmony with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

2. B — Red, blue, and yellow

3. D — The speed of the music

4. B — Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

5. B — Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

6. D — Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. C — Practise Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

8. A — Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk

9. D — Practise Kenyan Contemporary Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

10. D — Practise Contemporary Songs from Kenya with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

11. A — Practise Western Instruments with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. D — Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Kenyan Contemporary Songs; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Classical Music; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Music and Dance Industry; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Rhythm; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
